To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optical properties of MnAs layers depend on the crystallography of the layer.

the shape of EKE spectra of laser-deposited MnAs layers depends strongly on their crystallographic orientation and that the features in the energy dependance of the interband DOS of MnAs layers correspond to the energies obtained from calculations of MnAs band structure.

the shape of Kerr spectra of MnAs films depends on the crystal orientation and the spectra of GaAs-Mn composite films are similar to the spectra of MnAs and GaAs films, but with a smaller amplitude of the Kerr rotation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical and magneto-optic properties of MnAs layers, which are the basic elements in GaAs–MnAs heterostructures.
the investigation of the optical and magnetic properties of thin composite Ga _{1−x} Mn _{x} As films.
optical and magneto-optic properties of MnAs layers grown by laser deposition on GaAs substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of the MnAs layers, the EKE spectra are sensitive to the orientation of the layers and the interband density-of-states spectra are sensitive to crystallographic anisotropy.
the MnAs layer is a ferromagnetic semiconductor, and the MnAs layer and the GaAs layer are ferromagnetically coupled.
, for the first time, we have observed and studied the magneto-optical Kerr effect in the MnAs layers and composite GaAs-MgAs structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magneto-optical properties of MnAs layers can be explained by the presence of a large density of states of d-electrons in the MnAs valence band.
we have developed a technique for the preparation of high-quality GaAs-Mn layers and composites with a high Mn concentration.
the magneto-optical Kerr effect is an effective tool for studying the band structure and electronic properties of MnAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kerr effect in GaAs-Mn spin systems can be used for the study of the magnetic properties of thin films.

the EKE spectra and optical properties of MnAs layers are sensitive to the crystallographic structure of the layers and can be used to determine the crystallographic orientations of these layers in the composite structures.
the EKE spectra and the dielectric tensor components of the composite layers are determined by the EKE spectra, dielectric tensor components and the layer thicknesses of their constituents.
